item.question_text: A development team asks whether the AI management system standard will tell them which accuracy metric and cut-off value to use for a classifier. Regarding verification and validation of an AI system, what does the standard place on the organization?

options.text: The organization adopts the minimum error rates that the document publishes for each class of AI system.
The organization documents its verification and validation measures together with criteria for applying them.
The organization uses the testing tools and release criteria listed in the implementation guidance annex.
The organization obtains approval from designated management for its model evaluation metrics before release.

item.explanation: Control A.6.2.4 places the obligation at the management-system level: "The organization shall define and document verification and validation measures for the AI system and specify criteria for their use." The standard governs that the measures and their criteria exist and are documented; it does not supply metrics, thresholds or test methods.
item.key_support: The organization shall define and document verification and validation measures for the AI system and specify criteria for their use.

distractor_support.support: reliability and safety requirements of the AI system, including acceptable error rates for the AI system performance;
distractor_support.why_wrong: Acceptable error rates are something the organization sets in its own evaluation plan, not figures issued by the document.

distractor_support.support: The verification and validation measures can include, but are not limited to:
distractor_support.why_wrong: The annex offers illustrative implementation guidance rather than a mandated list of tools and criteria.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall obtain approval from the designated management for the AI risk treatment plan and for acceptance of the residual AI risks.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Designated management approval attaches to the risk treatment plan and residual risk acceptance, not to model evaluation metrics.

item.question_text: A general insurer is drafting the boundary of its AI management system. Its estate includes a fraud model built by its own data team, a lead-scoring feature switched on inside a licensed CRM, an assistant embedded in a purchased service-desk product, and a claims team experimenting with a public chatbot. The draft boundary reads: "AI systems engineered by the insurer's data team." On what basis should the drafting team reject that boundary?

options.text: Bought-in capability is handled through the supplier alignment process rather than the boundary, which is drawn around what the insurer itself engineers.
Interested-party requirements can be recorded in a separate register, which lets the bought-in capability sit outside the declared boundary.
The context determination reaches the purposes of AI systems the insurer merely uses, so the CRM feature and embedded assistant sit inside the boundary.
The boundary can remain unrecorded until an inventory of vendor features is finished, and be set down in documented form after that.

item.explanation: Clause 4.1 requires the organization to weigh the intended purpose of AI systems that are "developed, provided or used by the organization", and to determine its roles with respect to them; capability the insurer only uses (the CRM feature, the embedded assistant, the trialled chatbot) is therefore part of the context that feeds the boundary, so a boundary limited to in-house engineering omits most of the estate.
item.key_support: The organization shall consider the intended purpose of the AI systems that are developed, provided or used by the organization.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The supplier control governs how supplied products and services are used; it does not displace the context determination that brings used AI systems inside the boundary.

distractor_support.support: which of these requirements will be addressed through the AI management system
distractor_support.why_wrong: Interested-party requirements are an input to determining the boundary, not a substitute that allows used AI capability to be left outside it.

distractor_support.support: The scope shall be available as documented information.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The boundary has to be available as documented information, so deferring any record of it is not an option the standard allows.

item.question_text: A bank licenses a fraud-detection model from a vendor, hosts it on its own infrastructure, and uses a separate firm to prepare retraining data. Internal job descriptions exist for each AI team, but no party is named as owner of post-deployment drift monitoring. Reading the allocation-of-responsibilities control, how should the bank treat this gap?

options.text: Monitoring duties across the life cycle must be apportioned between the bank and the outside parties it works with.
Internal job descriptions can stand alone here, with the vendor's duties left to the contract owners to settle.
A confidential channel for raising concerns about the bank's role adequately addresses the unowned monitoring task.
Naming one manager with authority to report system performance upward adequately addresses the unowned monitoring task.

item.explanation: The allocation control (A.10.2) requires that life cycle responsibilities be shared out beyond the organization's own staff: "The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties." Drift monitoring after deployment is a life cycle responsibility, so it must be explicitly placed with the bank, the vendor or the data firm.
item.key_support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.

distractor_support.support: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Defining internal roles does not discharge the separate obligation to allocate life cycle responsibilities across suppliers and third parties.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.
distractor_support.why_wrong: A concern-reporting process is a channel for raising issues, not a mechanism that assigns ownership of a life cycle activity.

distractor_support.support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for:
distractor_support.why_wrong: Authority for conformity and performance reporting sits inside the organization and does not settle how duties are divided with the vendor and data firm.

item.question_text: An insurer's AI management system is scoped to its claims-automation division only. During preparation for certification, the team debates who counts as top management for the purpose of assigning AIMS responsibilities and authorities. Which reading is consistent with the definition used by the standard?

options.text: The leaders who direct and control the claims-automation division at its highest level count as top management.
The board directing the whole insurer counts as top management, irrespective of how the system scope is drawn.
The individual given authority to report on management system performance counts as top management for this purpose.
Any manager to whom divisional leaders pass authority and resources counts as top management from that point on.

item.explanation: The definition of top management (3.3) includes a note stating that "If the scope of the management system (3.4) covers only part of an organization, then top management refers to those who direct and control that part of the organization." With the scope limited to the claims-automation division, its highest-level directing leaders are top management.
item.key_support: If the scope of the management system (3.4) covers only part of an organization, then top management refers to those who direct and control that part of the organization.

distractor_support.support: Note 2 to entry: If the scope of the management system (3.4) covers only part of an organization, then top management refers to those who direct and control that part of the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The definition ties top management to the part of the organization the scope covers, not automatically to the enterprise-wide board.

distractor_support.support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The person who reports on performance receives an assignment from top management and reports to it, so is a different actor.

distractor_support.support: Note 1 to entry: Top management has the power to delegate authority and provide resources within the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Delegating authority and resources is something top management does; it does not convert the recipient into top management.

item.question_text: An insurer retrains its claims-triage model each quarter on records that field agents upload through a shared portal. During a review, the team finds that a subset of uploads was assembled by an outside party in a coordinated way, and that several batches were labelled by staff who had no triage training. Hardware, hosting and network controls are unchanged and operating normally. Which AI-specific risk source does this scenario most directly illustrate?

options.text: Faulty components, or moving a trained model across different systems, can be a source of risk.
A wide range of operating situations, leaving performance uncertain, can be a source of risk.
The material used to retrain the model, and the way it was collected, can be a source of risk.
Immature technology, with limits and drift not yet understood, can be a source of risk.

item.explanation: The scenario concerns both the content of the retraining data and the collection route through which it arrived. Annex C, risk sources related to machine learning, states that "The quality of data used for ML and the process used to collect data can be sources of risk, as they can impact objectives such as safety and robustness (e.g. due to issues in data quality or data poisoning)." Coordinated third-party submissions and untrained labelling are exactly this source, not an infrastructure or maturity concern.
item.key_support: The quality of data used for ML and the process used to collect data can be sources of risk, as they can impact objectives such as safety and robustness (e.g. due to issues in data quality or data poisoning).

distractor_support.support: Risk sources related to hardware include hardware errors based on defective components or transferring trained ML models between different systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The scenario states hardware and hosting are operating normally and no model transfer is described.

distractor_support.support: When AI systems operate in complex environments, where the range of situation is broad, there can be uncertainty on the performance and therefore a source of risk (e.g. complex environment of autonomous driving).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Nothing in the scenario points to a broad or unpredictable operating environment; the problem lies in the data pipeline.

distractor_support.support: Risk sources can be related to less mature technology due to unknown factors (e.g. system limitations and boundary conditions, performance drift), but also due to the more mature technology due to technology complacency.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The scenario identifies contaminated and poorly labelled inputs rather than the maturity level of the technology itself.

item.question_text: A lending organization deploys a purchased scoring model. Declined applicants ask why their applications failed, and the organization cannot describe, in terms a person can follow, which factors drove each result; the supplier treats this as proprietary. An outcome review found no difference in decline rates across applicant groups, no personal data left the organization, and change requests are handled within agreed timescales. Which AI-specific risk source is most directly present?

options.text: Being unable to give affected applicants understandable information about results can be a source of risk.
Harm to data subjects arising from disclosure of personal or sensitive records can be a source of risk.
Limited ability to alter the system to correct defects or meet new demands can be a source of risk.
Automated decision-making that bears unfairly on particular persons or groups can be a source of risk.

item.explanation: The scenario isolates an explainability gap: affected parties cannot be told what influenced the outcome. Annex C, lack of transparency and explainability, states that "The inability to provide appropriate information to interested parties can be a source of risk (i.e. in terms of trustworthiness and accountability of the organization)." The facts given rule out the privacy, maintainability and fairness sources.
item.key_support: The inability to provide appropriate information to interested parties can be a source of risk (i.e. in terms of trustworthiness and accountability of the organization).

distractor_support.support: The misuse or disclosure of personal and sensitive data (e.g. health records) can have harmful effects on data subjects.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The scenario states that no personal data left the organization, so no misuse or disclosure is in play.

distractor_support.support: Maintainability is related to the ability of the organization to handle modifications of the AI system in order to correct defects or adjust to new requirements.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Change requests are described as being handled within agreed timescales, so modification capability is not the issue.

distractor_support.support: The inappropriate application of AI systems for automated decision-making can be unfair to specific persons or groups of persons.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The outcome review found no difference in decline rates across groups, so the scenario does not evidence unfair treatment.

item.question_text: A provider has finished an AI risk assessment for a fielded system: risks were analysed, compared against the organization's criteria, and ranked for treatment. The provider now proposes a significant change — moving the system into a new jurisdiction and offering it to a different user population. Under the AI management system requirements, what does this situation call for?

options.text: Conducting an AI system impact assessment for the proposed change, alongside the risk assessment already done.
Relying on the risk analysis of consequences to individuals and societies to discharge the impact assessment duty.
Holding the impact assessment over to the next planned review cycle rather than addressing the proposed change.
Releasing the impact assessment findings to relevant interested parties before the proposed change may proceed.

item.explanation: The operational requirement on AI system impact assessments (clause 8.4) ties performance of the assessment to planned intervals and to proposed significant changes: “The organization shall perform AI system impact assessments according to 6.1.4 at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed to occur.” A completed risk assessment, which is anchored in the AI objectives and outputs prioritized risk levels, does not replace it; the impact assessment is separately required and its results feed the risk assessment.
item.key_support: The organization shall perform AI system impact assessments according to 6.1.4 at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed to occur.

distractor_support.support: assess the potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies that would result if the identified risks were to materialize;
distractor_support.why_wrong: The risk analysis does assess consequences to individuals and societies, but it is a separate obligation from the impact assessment and does not satisfy it.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall perform AI system impact assessments according to 6.1.4 at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed to occur.
distractor_support.why_wrong: A proposed significant change is itself a trigger, so waiting for the next planned interval misreads the timing.

distractor_support.support: Where appropriate, the result of the system impact assessment can be made available to relevant interested parties as defined by the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Making results available to interested parties is permitted where appropriate, not a precondition for proceeding with a change.

item.question_text: A team has finished treating the risks for two AI systems and is now finalising the organization's statement of applicability. Based on the definition of that document and its notes, what does the finished document have to show?

options.text: Every identified risk and the controls set up to address it, together with reasons for including or leaving out controls.
Every implementation guidance point drawn from Annex B, together with a reason for applying or skipping each point.
Every control in the Annex A reference table recorded as adopted for the organization's AI systems and objectives.
Every control left out with a stated reason, while the controls actually adopted are simply listed without reasons.

item.explanation: The definition of the statement of applicability (3.26) describes it as documentation of all necessary controls plus justification for their inclusion or exclusion, and Note 2 states that "All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability." So both the risks and their controls, with inclusion/exclusion reasoning, belong in the document.
item.key_support: All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability.

distractor_support.support: It provides information to support the implementation of the controls listed in Table A.1 and to meet the control objective, but organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability (see 6.1.3).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Implementation guidance does not have to be documented or justified in the statement of applicability, so listing each guidance point is not what the document is expected to show.

distractor_support.support: Not all the control objectives and controls listed in Table A.1 are required to be used, and the organization can design and implement their own controls (see 6.1.3).
distractor_support.why_wrong: The reference table is not a mandatory adoption list, so recording all of its controls as adopted misstates what the document shows.

distractor_support.support: statement of applicability documentation of all necessary controls (3.23) and justification for inclusion or exclusion of controls
distractor_support.why_wrong: Justification is expected for inclusion as well as exclusion, so adopted controls cannot be listed without reasons.

item.question_text: A lender is building and releasing a credit-scoring model. Its entire AI capability is one senior data scientist who will design the model, judge whether it is fit for use, and put it into production alone. Applying the standard's guidance on AI expertise, what does this staffing picture suggest?

options.text: It lacks the mix of dedicated specialists whose combined skills cover evaluating, building and releasing AI systems.
It is adequate for a single practitioner who holds all three of those skill areas at once.
It is adequate once training records for that practitioner are retained as evidence of competence.
It lacks expertise for the later life-cycle stages, while design and evaluation needs are already met.

item.explanation: The annex discussion of AI expertise points to a range of specialists with cross-disciplinary skills: "A selection of dedicated specialists with interdisciplinary skill sets and expertise in assessing, developing and deploying AI systems is needed." (C.2.2). A single individual covering assessment, development and deployment does not give that spread of expertise.
item.key_support: A selection of dedicated specialists with interdisciplinary skill sets and expertise in assessing, developing and deploying AI systems is needed.

distractor_support.support: A selection of dedicated specialists with interdisciplinary skill sets and expertise in assessing, developing and deploying AI systems is needed.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The expertise described is a selection of specialists with interdisciplinary skills, not one person wearing every hat.

distractor_support.support: Appropriate documented information shall be available as evidence of competence.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Holding competence evidence is a separate matter and does not create the spread of specialist expertise that is needed.

distractor_support.support: Different resources can be necessary at different stages of the AI system life cycle.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The gap is not confined to later stages; the assessment and development skills are also expected to come from a range of specialists.

item.question_text: An organization finishing resource identification for a fraud-detection system has recorded its datasets, its modelling tools and its computing platform. Its resource records list the project's engineers by name but say nothing about what they are able to do, and the records stop at go-live. Which addition does the control on human resources call for?

options.text: Records of the engineers' competences for build and deployment, with later stages captured in maintenance logs.
Records naming contracted third-party staff and their competences, in-house staff being held in personnel files.
Records of the people and their competences used from build through to retirement, including verification and integration.
Records of training certificates for the named engineers, standing in place of resource documentation for people.

item.explanation: Clause A.4.6 obliges the organization, as part of resource identification, to "document information about the human resources and their competences utilized for the development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning, as well as verification and integration of the AI system." Names alone, stopping at go-live, do not meet that.
item.key_support: As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the human resources and their competences utilized for the development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning, as well as verification and integration of the AI system.

distractor_support.support: As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the human resources and their competences utilized for the development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning, as well as verification and integration of the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The documentation spans operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning too, not just build and deployment.

distractor_support.support: Resources can be provided by the organization itself, by its customers or by third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The human resource documentation covers the people used for the AI system whoever provides them, so in-house staff are not excluded.

distractor_support.support: Appropriate documented information shall be available as evidence of competence.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Competence evidence is a distinct obligation and does not replace documenting the human resources and their competences as part of resource identification.

item.question_text: A manufacturer produced a single resource list when its vision-inspection AI was designed. The system is now in operation, needing different computing capacity and different people, and a periodic retraining activity has begun. Which approach fits the requirement on documenting resources?

options.text: Treat the design-stage list as the baseline and rely on change management to note any departures from it.
Identify and record the resources needed for the activities at each life-cycle stage and for other AI-related work.
Record the resources the manufacturer supplies itself and leave out those supplied by customers or suppliers.
Record data and computing resources for each stage, keeping tools and people as listed at the design stage.

item.explanation: Clause A.4.2 requires the organization to "identify and document relevant resources required for the activities at given AI system life cycle stages and other AI-related activities relevant for the organization." A one-off design-stage list does not cover operation or the retraining activity.
item.key_support: The organization shall identify and document relevant resources required for the activities at given AI system life cycle stages and other AI-related activities relevant for the organization.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall identify and document relevant resources required for the activities at given AI system life cycle stages and other AI-related activities relevant for the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Documentation is tied to the resources needed at the given life-cycle stages, so a frozen design-stage baseline does not satisfy it.

distractor_support.support: Resources can be provided by the organization itself, by its customers or by third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Resources may come from customers or third parties, so excluding externally provided resources leaves the documentation incomplete.

distractor_support.support: As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the tooling resources utilized for the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Tooling and human resources carry their own documentation controls and cannot be left at a superseded design-stage snapshot.

item.question_text: A company buys a pre-trained model and a data-labelling service from an outside vendor and uses both inside an AI system covered by its AI management system. Which action does the standard require of the company with respect to this vendor arrangement?

options.text: Put a process in place so that what it takes from vendors fits its own stance on responsible AI development and use.
Accept the vendor's own management system evidence in place of its own process where the vendor holds certification.
Hold life cycle responsibilities open until the vendor's deliverables have been received and accepted by the company.
Require the vendor to issue the statement of applicability covering the controls applied to the delivered work.

item.explanation: The supplier control (A.10.3) places the duty on the organization: it "shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems". The other options shift the duty to the vendor or delay allocation of responsibilities.
item.key_support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The obligation to have the process rests on the organization, not on evidence supplied by the vendor.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Life cycle responsibilities are to be allocated across the parties, not left undecided pending delivery.

distractor_support.support: f) produce a statement of applicability that contains the necessary controls [see b), c) and d)] and provide justification for inclusion and exclusion of controls.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The statement of applicability is produced by the organization through its risk treatment process, not by the vendor.

item.question_text: An AIMS process owner concludes that a process forming part of the AI management system needs to be modified to support a new deployment. How should the modification be handled?

options.text: It is worked through as a planned activity once the need for it has been determined.
It is enacted immediately and its consequences reviewed afterwards as an unintended change.
It is held back until AI objectives have been re-established at the relevant functions and levels.
It is handed to the supplier accountable for the affected stage of the AI system life cycle.

item.explanation: Planning of changes (6.3) states that when the need for changes to the AI management system is determined, "the changes shall be carried out in a planned manner". The distractors confuse planned with unintended changes, import the objective-setting requirement, or move the duty to a supplier.
item.key_support: When the organization determines the need for changes to the AI management system, the changes shall be carried out in a planned manner.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall control planned changes and review the consequences of unintended changes, taking action to mitigate any adverse effects, as necessary.
distractor_support.why_wrong: A change the organization has decided it needs is a planned change to be controlled, not an unintended one reviewed after the fact.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish AI objectives at relevant functions and levels.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Setting AI objectives is a separate planning requirement and is not a precondition for making a needed change.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Allocating life cycle responsibilities does not move the organization's duty to carry out management system changes in a planned way.

item.question_text: A company holds certification to ISO/IEC 27001 and is now extending its management system to cover the AI systems it develops. The team proposes carrying its existing support and operation machinery across unchanged. Which analysis of that proposal is defensible?

options.text: Competence has to be determined afresh for people whose work affects AI performance, with documented evidence retained.
Security-related controls have to be delivered inside the existing ISO/IEC 27001 programme rather than as separate AI controls.
Existing security-policy awareness briefings can stand in for making staff aware of the AI policy and its implications.
Operational control can reuse the existing process criteria without establishing criteria for the AI-related processes.

item.explanation: Clause 7.2 obliges the organization to "determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance" and to hold documented information as evidence of competence; an ISMS skills matrix addresses a different body of knowledge, so competence is an element that must be rebuilt rather than inherited. The other options misread permissive integration guidance as a requirement (D.2 says security-related controls 'can' be integrated), substitute security awareness for the AI-policy awareness content required by 7.3, and ignore 8.1's requirement to establish criteria for the AI processes and implement the controls determined for AI operation.
item.key_support: determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance

distractor_support.support: In this case, the way to implement controls which (partly) relate to information security in this document (see B.6.1.2) can be integrated with the organization’s implementation of ISO/IEC 27001.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Annex D.2 permits integration with an existing ISO/IEC 27001 implementation but does not oblige the organization to deliver security-related controls that way.

distractor_support.support: Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: — the AI policy (see 5.2); — their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, including the benefits of improved AI performance; — the implications of not conforming with the AI management system requirements.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The awareness content is specific to the AI policy and the AI management system, so security-policy briefings do not discharge it even though the delivery infrastructure can be shared.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall implement the controls determined according to 6.1.3 that are related to the operation of the AI management system (e.g. AI system development and usage life cycle related controls).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Operational control carries over in form only: criteria must be established for the AI processes and the AI-specific controls implemented and monitored.

item.question_text: A team is drafting its statement of applicability and asks how the reference control list in Annex A constrains the set of controls it documents. Which description fits the defined meaning of the statement of applicability?

options.text: It documents the necessary controls with reasons for including or excluding them, and may fall short of or go beyond the reference list, since the organization may add controls of its own.
It documents the necessary controls with reasons for including or excluding them, and also records which portions of the implementation guidance the organization chose to adopt.
It documents only the controls the organization has included, because reasons for leaving controls out are captured instead in the risk treatment plan approved by management.
It documents the controls drawn from the reference list, while controls the organization designs itself are recorded separately as additional risk treatment measures.

item.explanation: The definition in 3.26 describes the statement of applicability as documentation of all necessary controls plus justification for inclusion or exclusion, and its Note 1 states that organizations "may not require all controls listed in Annex A or may even exceed the list in Annex A with additional controls established by the organization itself". So the documented set can be smaller or larger than the reference list, and organization-designed controls belong in the same document.
item.key_support: Note 1 to entry: Organizations may not require all controls listed in Annex A or may even exceed the list in Annex A with additional controls established by the organization itself.

distractor_support.support: organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability (see 6.1.3)
distractor_support.why_wrong: Adoption of implementation guidance need not be documented or justified in the statement of applicability.

distractor_support.support: statement of applicability documentation of all necessary controls (3.23) and justification for inclusion or exclusion of controls
distractor_support.why_wrong: Justification for exclusion is part of the statement of applicability itself, not something displaced into the risk treatment plan.

distractor_support.support: All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Controls established by the organization itself are reflected in the same statement of applicability, not recorded separately from it.

item.question_text: A provider sets objectives that steer the responsible development of its AI systems and builds measures for achieving them into its development life cycle. Which Annex A control area addresses this concern?

options.text: Management guidance for AI system development, which covers development objectives and responsible design processes
Use of AI systems, which covers objectives and processes for responsible use of AI systems
Policies related to AI, which covers documenting a policy on developing or using AI systems
Internal organization, which covers defining and allocating AI roles and responsibilities

item.explanation: The management guidance area for AI system development carries the control requiring the organization to "identify and document objectives to guide the responsible development AI systems, and take those objectives into account and integrate measures to achieve them in the development life cycle" (A.6.1.2). The other areas address use-side objectives, policy documentation and role allocation respectively.
item.key_support: A.6.1.2 Objectives for responsible developThe organization shall identify and document objectives ment of AI system to guide the responsible development AI systems, and take those objectives into account and integrate measures to achieve them in the development life cycle.

distractor_support.support: A.9.3 Objectives for responsible use of AI The organization shall identify and document objectives to system guide the responsible use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: That area sets objectives for responsible use, not for development and its life cycle measures.

distractor_support.support: A.2.2 AI policy The organization shall document a policy for the development or use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: That area concerns documenting and reviewing the AI policy rather than development objectives integrated into the life cycle.

distractor_support.support: A.3.2 AI roles and responsibilities Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: That area allocates accountability and handles reporting of concerns, not development objectives.

item.question_text: A bank has published an AI policy, assigned owners for each AI system, and listed the data, tooling and computing resources behind its credit-scoring model. During an internal audit it emerges that the bank's long-standing privacy, information security and quality policies were drafted before any AI work began and have never been examined against what the bank now wants to achieve with AI. Which Annex A control category directly addresses this gap?

options.text: Establishing where the firm's existing policies bear on, or are touched by, its AI aims
Setting a schedule for re-examining the AI policy so it stays suitable and effective
Producing a written policy covering how the firm builds or makes use of AI systems
Assigning accountabilities for AI work across the firm according to what it needs

item.explanation: The gap is that other corporate policies have never been checked against the organization's AI objectives. Control A.2.3 (Alignment with other organizational policies) states the organization "shall determine where other policies can be affected by or apply to, the organization’s objectives with respect to AI systems." The other options describe controls the bank has already satisfied or that address a different concern.
item.key_support: The organization shall determine where other policies can be affected by or apply to, the organization’s objectives with respect to AI systems.

distractor_support.support: The AI policy shall be reviewed at planned intervals or additionally as needed to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Review cycles keep the AI policy itself current; they do not cover the examination of other corporate policies against the AI objectives.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall document a policy for the development or use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The bank has already published an AI policy, so the documenting control is not the one left unaddressed.

distractor_support.support: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Owners have already been assigned for each AI system, and role allocation says nothing about reconciling pre-existing policies with AI objectives.

item.question_text: A development team finishes building a fraud-scoring model. Test methods and pass/fail thresholds had been written down and executed, and a monitoring rota is scheduled for go-live. However, the model is pushed into production with no written release plan, and nobody checked whether the agreed pre-release conditions and sign-offs had actually been satisfied. Which Annex A control would most directly have prevented this failure?

options.text: Recording a plan for release and confirming the conditions due before it
Setting out test and evaluation measures together with criteria for their use
Fixing the elements needed to keep the system running day to day
Writing down the specification for a newly built or reworked system

item.explanation: Control A.6.2.5 (AI system deployment) covers exactly this gap: "The organization shall document a deployment plan and ensure that appropriate requirements are met prior to deployment." The scenario shows no deployment plan and no confirmation of pre-deployment conditions.
item.key_support: The organization shall document a deployment plan and ensure that appropriate requirements are met prior to deployment.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and document verification and validation measures for the AI system and specify criteria for their use.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The team had already defined and applied documented test measures and criteria, so this control was satisfied.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and document the necessary elements for the ongoing operation of the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: This control addresses the post-release operating stage, not the release gate that was skipped.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall specify and document requirements for new AI systems or material enhancements to existing systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The failure occurred at the transition into production, not in specifying the system at the outset.

item.question_text: A supervisory authority asks an AI provider for records of the inputs and outputs handled by a deployed triage system during three months of live service. The provider can produce event records from its development and test environments only; it had never worked out for which life-cycle phases such records would be captured, and nothing was captured in production. Which Annex A control does this situation fail to satisfy?

options.text: Deciding for which life-cycle phases event records are captured, with live use as the floor
Working out which technical documentation each category of interested party needs
Setting out monitoring, repair, update and support arrangements for the running system
Recording design and build decisions against the agreed specification criteria

item.explanation: A.6.2.8 places a determination duty on the organization about the phases in which event logs are kept, and names the in-use phase as the minimum: "The organization shall determine at which phases of the AI system life cycle, record keeping of event logs should be enabled, but at the minimum when the AI system is in use." The provider made no such determination and captured nothing in live use.
item.key_support: The organization shall determine at which phases of the AI system life cycle, record keeping of event logs should be enabled, but at the minimum when the AI system is in use.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine what AI system technical documentation is needed for each relevant category of interested parties, such as users, partners, supervisory authorities, and provide the technical documentation to them in the appropriate form.
distractor_support.why_wrong: This control concerns supplying technical documentation to interested parties, not keeping operational event records.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and document the necessary elements for the ongoing operation of the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Operation and monitoring covers the elements of running the system, while the specific record-keeping determination sits in the event log control.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall document the AI system design and development based on organizational objectives, documented requirements and specification criteria.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Design and development documentation concerns build-time decisions rather than records of events in service.

item.question_text: An organization has an established and followed procedure for judging the consequences of its AI systems, and the outcomes are filed and kept for the period its retention schedule sets. An internal audit of a news-recommendation system finds that every assessment entry addresses harms to named users and user groups; effects such as the spread of misinformation, energy consumption and pressure on public debate were never examined at any stage of the system's life. Which Annex A control is not being met?

options.text: Examining and recording how the system can affect society across its life
Examining and recording effects on individuals and groups across the system's life
Recording the outcomes of assessments and keeping them for a set period
Putting in place the procedure for judging possible consequences of the system

item.explanation: A.5.5 requires the societal dimension specifically: "The organization shall assess and document the potential societal impacts of their AI systems throughout their life cycle." Misinformation, environmental and public-debate effects are societal impacts that were never assessed.
item.key_support: The organization shall assess and document the potential societal impacts of their AI systems throughout their life cycle.

distractor_support.support: impacts of AI systems to individuals or groups of individuals throughout the system’s life cycle
distractor_support.why_wrong: Impacts on individuals and groups were assessed; the untouched dimension is the societal one.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall document the results of AI system impact assessments and retain results for a defined period.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Results are documented and retained for a defined period, so this control is satisfied.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish a process to assess the potential consequences for individuals or groups of individuals, or both, and societies that can result from the AI system throughout its life cycle.
distractor_support.why_wrong: A process is already established and used; the shortfall lies in the societal assessment actually performed.

item.question_text: A financial regulator in the organization's jurisdiction has statutory power to demand technical documentation, impact assessment results and system logs from operators of the credit-scoring AI system the organization runs. Applying the Annex A transparency controls, what does the organization do about this?

options.text: Set out in writing its reporting duties toward outside parties such as regulators.
Open a channel through which outside parties can flag harmful effects of the system.
Draw up a written plan for telling system users when incidents occur.
Work out and hand over the information that users of the system need.

item.explanation: The control on information for interested parties (A.8.5) is the one that addresses duties owed to parties such as regulators: the organization "shall determine and document their obligations to reporting information about the AI system to interested parties." The other options are different transparency controls aimed at inbound reports, incident notices or user-facing information.
item.key_support: The organization shall determine and document their obligations to reporting information about the AI system to interested parties.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall provide capabilities for interested parties to report adverse impacts of the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: This control concerns reports coming in from interested parties, not information the organization owes outward to a regulator.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine and document a plan for communicating incidents to users of the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: An incident communication plan is directed at users and is triggered by incidents, not by a standing regulatory reporting duty.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine and provide the necessary information to users of the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: This control addresses information supplied to users of the system rather than obligations to report to authorities.

item.question_text: Before training a demand-forecasting model, a development team buys a third-party dataset, fills missing entries by imputation, normalizes two variables and encodes categorical fields as numbers. Which Annex A data requirement obliges the team to record the basis on which these handling techniques were chosen?

options.text: Documented criteria for choosing the data preparation steps and methods used.
Documented details of how the dataset was acquired and selected for the system.
Documented data quality requirements, with assurance that the data satisfy them.
A documented process for recording where the data came from across life cycles.

item.explanation: Imputation, normalization and encoding are data preparation steps, and the data preparation control (A.7.6) requires the organization to "define and document its criteria for selecting data preparations and the data preparation methods to be used." The other options are neighbouring data controls covering acquisition, quality and provenance.
item.key_support: The organization shall define and document its criteria for selecting data preparations and the data preparation methods to be used.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine and document details about the acquisition and selection of the data used in AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Acquisition documentation covers sources, quantity and rights of the data obtained, not the rationale for the transformations applied to it.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and document requirements for data quality and ensure that data used to develop and operate the AI system meet those requirements.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Quality requirements state the standard the data must reach, not the criteria for picking particular preparation techniques.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and document a process for recording the provenance of data used in its AI systems over the life cycles of the data and the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Provenance recording traces the origin and handling history of data rather than justifying the choice of preparation methods.

item.question_text: People affected by an automated benefits-eligibility system have begun complaining through unofficial routes that its decisions are unfair, because the organization offers them no way to raise such concerns. Which Annex A control gap does this situation point to?

options.text: No means for interested parties to report harmful effects of the system.
No documented plan for notifying system users when incidents arise.
No documented statement of duties to report system details to authorities.
No determination of the information to be given to users of the system.

item.explanation: The external reporting control (A.8.3) is the gap: the organization "shall provide capabilities for interested parties to report adverse impacts of the AI system." The distractors are other transparency controls dealing with incident notification, outward reporting obligations and user information.
item.key_support: The organization shall provide capabilities for interested parties to report adverse impacts of the AI system.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine and document a plan for communicating incidents to users of the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: An incident communication plan pushes information out to users; it does not give affected parties a route to report unfairness.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine and document their obligations to reporting information about the AI system to interested parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: This control concerns the organization's own outward reporting duties, not the receiving of complaints about adverse impacts.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine and provide the necessary information to users of the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Providing information to users addresses understanding of the system, not a feedback capability for reporting harms.

item.question_text: A retailer licenses a CV-screening AI tool from a vendor and runs it internally for its own hiring. It builds no AI systems and sells no AI products or services. While deciding which reference controls to implement for use and for relationships, which action best fits the retailer's role?

options.text: Put in place a process so that what the vendor supplies is consistent with the retailer's responsible approach to using AI.
Leave the whole relationships category out of scope, as the retailer neither builds nor supplies any AI system.
Take the published list of responsible-use objectives, such as fairness and explainability, as the complete set the retailer has to adopt.
Treat the hiring managers who receive the tool's shortlists as the customers whose expectations the relationships category addresses.

item.explanation: The supplier control (A.10.3) is framed around the organization's own usage of items obtained from suppliers, so it applies to an organization that only deploys a purchased tool: "The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems." (A.10.3)
item.key_support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The supplier control is written about the organization's usage of supplier-provided items, so a purely deploying organization is squarely within its reach.

distractor_support.support: Depending on its context, the organization should identify its objectives related to responsible use.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The named qualities are offered as examples in guidance phrased with 'should', not as a fixed set the organization has to adopt.

distractor_support.support: The organization should understand customer expectations and needs when it is supplying a product or service related to an AI system (i.e. when it is itself a supplier).
distractor_support.why_wrong: The customer control concerns those to whom the organization supplies an AI-related product or service, not internal staff using a purchased tool.

item.question_text: A software firm already operates a certified information security management system and is now building an AI management system. Its lead auditor asks how far the existing security work can be reused. Which statement best reflects Annex D's position on this situation?

options.text: Work on AI management system controls that bear partly on information security may be carried out together with the firm's existing ISO/IEC 27001 implementation.
Privacy-related objectives and controls of the AI management system may be folded into the firm's existing ISO/IEC 27001 implementation.
Access protection already applied to the deployed model's interface discharges the obligation to record where its training data came from.
Security work for the AI components is kept apart from the security work covering the remaining components of the system.

item.explanation: Annex D.2 states that where an organization has an ISO/IEC 27001 implementation, "the way to implement controls which (partly) relate to information security in this document (see B.6.1.2) can be integrated with the organization’s implementation of ISO/IEC 27001." Integration is contemplated for the security-related portion of the AI controls.
item.key_support: In this case, the way to implement controls which (partly) relate to information security in this document (see B.6.1.2) can be integrated with the organization’s implementation of ISO/IEC 27001.

distractor_support.support: Privacy-related objectives and controls of the AI management system (see B.2.3 and B.5.4) can be integrated with the organization’s implementation of ISO/IEC 27701.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Annex D pairs the privacy-related objectives and controls with ISO/IEC 27701, not with ISO/IEC 27001.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and document a process for recording the provenance of data used in its AI systems over the life cycles of the data and the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Provenance recording is a separate documented process and is not delivered by protecting access to the model.

distractor_support.support: Objectives such as safety, security, privacy and environmental impact should be managed holistically and not separately for AI and the other components of the system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Annex D.1 points the other way, toward managing security across the whole system rather than separating the AI part.

item.question_text: A machine learning team argues that because its models run on infrastructure already hardened under the organization's information security programme, no further security analysis is warranted for the models themselves. Which response is best supported by the guidance on security objectives for AI?

options.text: Security questions arising specifically from machine learning approaches merit consideration in addition to conventional information and system security matters.
Coverage of the hosting infrastructure by conventional information security measures is treated as settling the security question for the models.
Security for the model components is best handled as a separate exercise from security for the surrounding components.
An information security management system conforming to ISO/IEC 27001 has to be in place before AI security objectives can be addressed.

item.explanation: Annex C's guidance on security states that for AI, and particularly for ML-based systems, "new security issues should be considered beyond classical information and system security concerns" (C.2.10). Existing infrastructure hardening does not exhaust those considerations.
item.key_support: In the context of AI and in particular with regard to AI systems based on ML approaches, new security issues should be considered beyond classical information and system security concerns.

distractor_support.support: In the context of AI and in particular with regard to AI systems based on ML approaches, new security issues should be considered beyond classical information and system security concerns.
distractor_support.why_wrong: It equates classical security coverage with the full set of security issues that ML approaches raise.

distractor_support.support: Objectives such as safety, security, privacy and environmental impact should be managed holistically and not separately for AI and the other components of the system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Annex D.1 recommends holistic handling rather than a security exercise split off for the AI parts.

distractor_support.support: If an organization identifies the need to implement an AI management system and to address security objectives in a similar thorough and systematic way, it can implement an information security management system in conformity with ISO/IEC 27001.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Annex D.2 presents ISO/IEC 27001 implementation as an option the organization can take, not a precondition.

item.question_text: An organization's AI risk assessment identifies a risk that is addressed by a control it will implement jointly with its existing information security programme. When the organization prepares its statement of applicability, how should this risk and control be handled?

options.text: Both the identified risk and the measure put in place to address it are reflected in the statement of applicability.
Controls delivered through the existing security programme are recorded in that programme's documentation instead.
The listing is confined to controls reproduced in Annex A, with organization-defined controls held elsewhere.
Reasoning is recorded for the controls that were left out, while controls brought in need no accompanying rationale.

item.explanation: The definition of the statement of applicability requires that "All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability" (3.26, Note 2). Implementing a control jointly with another management system does not remove it from the AI statement of applicability.
item.key_support: All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability.

distractor_support.support: All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Shared implementation with another management system does not relieve the organization of reflecting the risk and control in this statement of applicability.

distractor_support.support: Note 1 to entry: Organizations may not require all controls listed in Annex A or may even exceed the list in Annex A with additional controls established by the organization itself.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Controls established by the organization beyond Annex A also belong in the statement of applicability.

distractor_support.support: statement of applicability documentation of all necessary controls (3.23) and justification for inclusion or exclusion of controls
distractor_support.why_wrong: Justification accompanies inclusion as well as exclusion of controls.

item.question_text: An AIMS team is choosing an indicator that speaks to the effectiveness of its AI management system, rather than to some other concept used in the terminology of AI management systems. Which description corresponds to effectiveness?

options.text: The extent to which the activities the organization planned are carried out and the results it planned for are obtained.
The determination of the status of a system, a process or an activity, through checking or observing it.
The process the organization carries out in order to arrive at a value for a characteristic of interest.
The score an AI model achieves against a chosen technical metric, such as an agreed F1 value.

item.explanation: The terminology entry for effectiveness (3.13) reads "effectiveness extent to which planned activities are realized and planned results are achieved", so an effectiveness indicator asks whether what was planned happened and delivered the intended results. The other options describe monitoring (3.20), measurement (3.19) and a technical model performance metric discussed in the operation and monitoring guidance (B.6.2.6).
item.key_support: effectiveness extent to which planned activities are realized and planned results are achieved

distractor_support.support: monitoring determining the status of a system, a process (3.8) or an activity
distractor_support.why_wrong: This is the definition of monitoring, which establishes current status rather than whether planned activities and results were achieved.

distractor_support.support: measurement process (3.8) to determine a value
distractor_support.why_wrong: This is the definition of measurement, the act of determining a value, not the concept of effectiveness.

distractor_support.support: For example, an organization can determine that the F1 score is an appropriate performance metric based on its assessment of the impact of false positives and false negatives, as described in ISO/IEC TS 4213.
distractor_support.why_wrong: An F1 score is a technical performance metric for an AI system, which is a different concept from the realization of planned activities and results.

item.question_text: A deployed recruitment-screening AI system began rejecting candidates in a protected group at a much higher rate, breaching an internal fairness requirement. Investigation showed a vendor-supplied training dataset had been labelled using an outdated scheme, and the organization's intake checks never tested labelling consistency. The team: (i) switched screening to manual review and told affected applicants, (ii) relabelled the dataset and redeployed a retrained model, (iii) added a labelling-consistency acceptance test to the vendor data intake process and required vendor sign-off, (iv) logged the incident and the results in its records. Using the definition of corrective action, which one of these is the corrective action?

options.text: Adding a labelling-consistency acceptance test with vendor sign-off to the data intake process
Relabelling the affected dataset and redeploying a retrained screening model
Switching screening to manual review and informing the affected applicants
Logging the incident details and the outcome of the actions in the organization's records

item.explanation: The vocabulary entry for corrective action (3.17) describes it as "action to eliminate the cause(s) of a nonconformity (3.16) and to prevent recurrence". Only the new intake acceptance test with vendor sign-off addresses the cause (uncontrolled supplier labelling) so the failure does not come back; the other three are correction, handling of consequences, and record keeping.
item.key_support: corrective action action to eliminate the cause(s) of a nonconformity (3.16) and to prevent recurrence

distractor_support.support: take action to control and correct it
distractor_support.why_wrong: Relabelling the data and redeploying the model corrects the nonconforming output itself, which is correction rather than elimination of the cause.

distractor_support.support: deal with the consequences
distractor_support.why_wrong: Manual review and applicant notification handle the consequences of the failure and do not remove its cause.

distractor_support.support: Documented information shall be available as evidence of:
distractor_support.why_wrong: Recording the nonconformity and the results is evidence of what was done, not an action that eliminates the cause.

item.question_text: In the AI management system standard's terminology, a management system is best understood as which of the following?

options.text: Connected organizational elements that set policies and objectives, together with the processes used to reach them.
Documented audit procedures that a certification body follows when it evaluates a client organization.
An agreed programme of initial, surveillance and recertification audits covering a three-year period.
Declared arrangements for impartiality and auditor competence held by the body issuing certificates.

item.explanation: The definition in the terms clause (3.4) describes a management system as "set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization (3.1) to establish policies (3.5) and objectives (3.6), as well as processes (3.8) to achieve those objectives". Audit programmes, certificate cycles and certification-body impartiality belong to the conformity assessment documents, not to this definition.
item.key_support: management system set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization (3.1) to establish policies (3.5) and objectives (3.6), as well as processes (3.8) to achieve those objectives

distractor_support.support: This document specifies the requirements and provides guidance for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI (artificial intelligence) management system within the context of an organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The document addresses the organization's own management system, so audit procedures used by a certifier are not what the term denotes.

distractor_support.support: This document is intended for use by an organization providing or using products or services that utilize AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: An audit cycle is an activity of a certification scheme and is not part of the defined term.

distractor_support.support: organization person or group of people that has its own functions with responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve its objectives (3.6)
distractor_support.why_wrong: Impartiality and competence arrangements sit with the certifying body, not within the organization's defined management system.

item.question_text: A manager wants to run one system covering AI together with information security and quality. What does the terminology note accompanying the definition of a management system indicate about the disciplines covered?

options.text: It can cover a single discipline or extend across several of them.
It has to be limited to AI alone if the organization seeks certification.
It is settled by the certification body when audit time is calculated.
It is determined by the accreditation body that assesses the certifier.

item.explanation: Note 1 to entry in the terms clause (3.4) states that "A management system can address a single discipline or several disciplines." The other options transfer the decision to a certifier or accreditation body, or invent a single-discipline restriction that the definition does not impose.
item.key_support: Note 1 to entry: A management system can address a single discipline or several disciplines.

distractor_support.support: Note 1 to entry: A management system can address a single discipline or several disciplines.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The note expressly allows several disciplines, so no single-discipline restriction applies.

distractor_support.support: This document specifies the requirements and provides guidance for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI (artificial intelligence) management system within the context of an organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Scope of disciplines is an organizational choice under the definition, not an output of a certifier's audit time calculation.

distractor_support.support: Note 2 to entry: If the organization is part of a larger entity, the term “organization” refers only to the part of the larger entity that is within the scope of the AI management system (3.4).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Boundaries relate to the organization itself; an accreditation body assesses certifiers, not the disciplines an organization chooses to cover.

item.question_text: According to the terminology note on management system elements, which grouping is identified as part of a management system?

options.text: Auditor competence criteria and the impartiality safeguards applied by a certifying body.
The organization's structure, its roles and responsibilities, and its planning and operation.
The two-stage initial audit and the surveillance activity that follows certification.
The scope of accreditation granted to the body that issues the certificate.

item.explanation: Note 2 to entry in the terms clause (3.4) states that "The management system elements include the organization’s structure, roles and responsibilities, planning and operation." Auditor competence, audit staging and accreditation scope are features of the conformity assessment arrangements, not elements of the organization's management system.
item.key_support: The management system elements include the organization’s structure, roles and responsibilities, planning and operation.

distractor_support.support: This document specifies the requirements and provides guidance for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI (artificial intelligence) management system within the context of an organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Competence and impartiality of auditors are attributes of a certification body, not listed elements of the organization's system.

distractor_support.support: Note 2 to entry: The management system elements include the organization’s structure, roles and responsibilities, planning and operation.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The listed elements are organizational; audit staging and surveillance are not among them.

distractor_support.support: organization person or group of people that has its own functions with responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve its objectives (3.6)
distractor_support.why_wrong: Accreditation scope describes the certifier that was assessed, not an element inside the organization being examined.

item.question_text: An implementer claims that the definition of a management system in the AI management system standard tells them how their certification audit will be sequenced. Which response is best supported?

options.text: The definition states that the initial audit is carried out in two stages before any certificate is granted.
The definition fixes the length of time for which a certificate granted against the standard stays valid.
The definition sets the competence that an audit team leader must hold for these audits.
The definition covers organizational elements that set policies and objectives and the processes to meet them.

item.explanation: The defined term in clause 3.4 is about the organization's own arrangements: "set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization (3.1) to establish policies (3.5) and objectives (3.6), as well as processes (3.8) to achieve those objectives". Audit staging, certificate validity and audit team competence are matters for the conformity assessment documents, not this definition.
item.key_support: management system set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization (3.1) to establish policies (3.5) and objectives (3.6), as well as processes (3.8) to achieve those objectives

distractor_support.support: This document specifies the requirements and provides guidance for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI (artificial intelligence) management system within the context of an organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The document's subject is the organization's management system, so audit staging is not addressed by the definition.

distractor_support.support: This document is applicable to any organization, regardless of size, type and nature, that provides or uses products or services that utilize AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Nothing in the definition or scope deals with how long a certificate remains valid.

distractor_support.support: organization person or group of people that has its own functions with responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve its objectives (3.6)
distractor_support.why_wrong: Responsibilities and authorities here are those of the organization, not competence rules for an external audit team.
